name: Cowpea Weevil (Cowpea Bruchid)
description: A major storage pest of cowpea that develops inside stored seeds. Adult females lay eggs on pods or seeds, and larvae develop within, completely hollowing out seeds. It can cause total loss of stored cowpea within months.
symptoms: Small round exit holes on stored seeds
Eggs visible on seed surface as small white dots
Fine seed dust at bottom of storage containers
Seeds hollowed out and reduced to shells
Adults emerging and flying in storage containers
Seed weight and quality severely reduced
treatments: Mix stored cowpea with food-grade vegetable oil (5ml/kg seed)
Use hermetic storage methods (double bagging with Purdue Improved Cowpea Storage bags)
Apply food-grade diatomaceous earth to stored grain
Mix with neem leaf powder or neem oil (5-10ml/kg)
Freeze seeds at -18°C for 72 hours to kill all life stages
prevention: Harvest pods before they dry and split in the field
Dry seeds thoroughly (to <12% moisture) before storage
Store in airtight or hermetic containers
Treat seeds with botanical protectants (neem oil, chili pepper dust)
Clean storage area thoroughly before introducing new harvest
Store only completely dry, undamaged seeds
